zara_devx: Quick report: AsyncClient losing correlation/request-id when retry/backoff runs or when the OTEL instrumentor is active. Small repro below.

zara_devx: ```py
# repro: asyncio + contextvars + redwood async client
import asyncio
from contextvars import ContextVar
from redwood import AsyncClient
req = ContextVar('request_id')
async def main():
    req.set('trace-900')
    c = AsyncClient(retry_policy={'max_attempts':2}, instrumentor_enabled=True)
    await c.generate_async('test')  # logs for attempt 2 show empty request_id
asyncio.run(main())
```

leo_sdk: Thanks for the repro. We suspect the backoff/retry code path spawns child tasks without copying the caller context (contextvars). We also recently moved an exporter path to anyio TaskGroup which might explain the OTEL interaction.

maya_obs: If true, two-pronged fix: 1) centralise task spawn to always use context.copy_context().run(asyncio.create_task, coro) so contextvars persist, 2) add a small observability hook API so integrators can opt-in to rebind/emit additional metadata in the SDK lifecycle (emit_log/span_start/retry).

zara_devx: Hook idea sounds good 94 what's a minimal, well-typed shape that works for both sync and async callables?

leo_sdk: Proposal: a Protocol-based callback shape so typing stays nice: 
```
from typing import Protocol, Mapping, Optional, Awaitable
class ObsCallback(Protocol):
    def __call__(self, event: str, attrs: Mapping[str,str]) -> Optional[Awaitable[None]]: ...
```
Client.register_observer(event: str, cb: ObsCallback) would accept either sync or async callables; client will call cb(...) and await if it returns an awaitable.

maya_obs: Nice. Also add small convenience helpers: bind_contextvar(name: str, var: ContextVar) and instrument_opentelemetry(baggage_map: Callable[[Dict], Dict]) to make common integrations trivial. Include examples in SDK docs.

drew_infra: Long-term: audit all spawn sites (retry/backoff, batcher, token refresh, exporter) and switch to a single _spawn_task helper that preserves contextvars. Short-term: the hook API gives integrators a supported escape hatch.

zara_devx: For a quick workaround I wrapped the hook to snapshot and restore the contextvar around calls. Ugly but works: 
```
def snapshot_cb(cb, var):
    async def wrapped(*a, **k):
        token = var.set(var.get(None))
        try:
            r = cb(*a, **k)
            if hasattr(r, '__await__'):
                await r
        finally:
            var.reset(token)
    return wrapped
```

leo_sdk: Good proof-of-concept. Implementation plan from SDK side: 1) add ObsCallback Protocol + register_observer; 2) add _spawn_task(ctx, coro) helper and migrate a subset of hotspots; 3) add bind_contextvar and instrument_opentelemetry helpers; 4) integration test in devex/sample-apps/tests to assert logs and OTEL spans keep the request_id across retries.

maya_obs: The integration test should force a transient error so retry runs, then assert both the emitted logs and the OTEL span/baggage contain the request_id. Put the test in CI so we don't regress. Also include a short performance note: awaiting observer callbacks on hot paths can add latency, so document sync vs async tradeoffs.

drew_infra: I'll prototype the spawn helper and replace the retry/backoff spawn point in a small PR. Keep the hooking surface for follow-up to reduce surface area for the quick patch.

zara_devx: Thanks 94 I'll add the failing log snippets and the tiny repro into the issue so the PR has a repro harness. If helpful I can also paste a small sample-app test.

leo_sdk: Please do. Tagging @maya_obs for test expectations. Once spawn helper lands we'll follow up with the typed observer API and adapters.

maya_obs: One last note: when documenting instrument_opentelemetry(), call out that some OTEL instrumentors rely on contextvar-only propagation; recommend copying OTEL baggage into contextvars when users rely on application ContextVars for correlation. That avoids surprises.

zara_devx: Filed the sample test in the issue. Thanks all!"
